stops.note: origin disputed even in antiquity: in Ovid's Fasti, Juno claims the month for herself while Juventas claims it for the iuniores, the young men
gave Middle English june, replacing Old English Ærra Liþa, 'the earlier mild month'
reinforced by Latin Iunius in learned writing; Magna Carta was sealed at Runnymede on 15 June 1215

current_meaning: the sixth month of the year
